subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw expand the stable core config contract to accept `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml`, or keep JSON/JSON5 canonical and address editing friction through CLI, Control UI, and `config.patch` guidance?
rationale: The request changes a stable on-disk config contract and needs human product ownership for parser behavior, precedence when multiple files exist, write-back format, validation, and upgrade/doctor expectations.

options.title: Keep JSON/JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve supported comment-aware mutation guidance instead.

options.title: Sponsor YAML Support
options.body: Accept YAML only with explicit parser, precedence, docs, fresh-install, upgrade, and doctor proof requirements.

options.title: Split Mutation Guidance
options.body: Track a narrower docs or agent-prompt item for avoiding raw parse-and-dump edits without adding a second config format.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON/JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve supported comment-aware mutation guidance instead.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about config compatibility and doctor/recovery policy, where recent history points most strongly to this owner area.
